prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign PISCES: two fish circling each other head to tail, like a yin and yang: one swims up on the left, the other swims down on the right, each a simple curved fish with a round eye, fan tail and rows of rounded scales. A fine cord runs in a loose curve from the mouth of one to the mouth of the other, joining them.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, soft rolling waves, rising bubbles and long strands of sea weed spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, balanced by rotation: turn it half round and it looks the same, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. It is an animal: absolutely NO human face. Their faces are calm and neutral with a steady level gaze: no open mouth, no snarl, no frown. The sign's nature shows only through form: two flowing curves that answer each other, soft rounded scales, no hard corners: compassion, imagination, dreaming, two currents in one sea.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: pearl white, sea green, soft indigo, coral pink. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
